It conveys the belief that the ultimate reality is beyond the tangible world and that there exists a divine force that governs the universe.

historical_references.reference: The name 'Trilokesh' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'triloka' meaning 'three worlds' and 'ish' meaning 'lord'. This name was used to describe the Hindu deity Vishnu in his role as the controller of the three worlds - the physical world, the heavenly world, and the netherworld. This usage can be traced back to ancient Hindu scriptures such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

Trilokesh was also the name of a legendary king in Hindu mythology, who ruled over the three worlds - the heavens, the earth, and the netherworld. This king is believed to have reigned during the Treta Yuga, a period of great prosperity and happiness in Hindu mythology. He is often described as a just and virtuous ruler who upheld the moral order of the universe and protected his subjects from harm.
